title: Who makes the maker?

data.source: Rosen's (M,R)-systems (1991) and autopoiesis (Maturana and Varela 1980). Computed: a brute-force count on finite sets, a noiseless seed-coupled rotor knocked seven ways, and a three-catalyst ring.

prediction: A CRR loop rebuilds its own seed and nothing else. Its drive, friction, half-turn, coupling and carry-over are set from outside and stay wherever a knock leaves them. Nothing in it wears out, so nothing in it needs rebuilding. An autocatalytic ring rebuilds every part that wears. So the loop has one small piece of Rosen's closure and not the rest.
baseline: Closure to efficient causation (Rosen 1991) and autopoiesis (Maturana and Varela 1980), with a three-catalyst ring as the worked example. Decoy: a clock with no seed.
why: Not every prediction held: P2_only_the_seed_is_restored. Mixed: the seed is rebuilt from inside, the other six makers are not. Shared: a loop in which something made by the process shapes the process (R5, and the coupling in R4, each carry the status ASSUMPTION in Phoenix). Left over on Rosen's side: makers that wear out and are remade, all the way round. Left over on CRR's side: a ruler and a clock.
weighs: Facts about the models as written.
result: Rosen's count: of 16 repair maps on two inputs and two outputs, 4 can be told apart from one output (0.25); with three, 27 of 19683. In the CRR loop a knock to the seed halved every 3.67 occasions (formula 1.94) and the seed came back; knocks to the drive, friction, half-turn, potential, coupling and carry-over stayed for good, shifting the occasion's length by -0.3112, 0.7333, 0.7333, 1.7339, 0.0026 and 0.0. Restored: 1 of 7. The ring settled at 0.7517, restored all 3 catalysts after a knock in 2.22 time units, came back to 1.0 of its level after total removal with a trickle of spontaneous making, and stayed dead without it. In my variant the knocked coupling was back to 1.0 of its value. Not every prediction of mine held: P2 missed; see the limits.

precise_core: The (M,R) scheme is defined with sets and maps. Rosen's main theorem, that such systems cannot be simulated, is disputed. Autopoiesis is prose with computer models.
proved_by_others: Worked over by independent groups (Letelier, Cardenas, Cornish-Bowden; Louie; Mossio) and by critics.
differing_prediction: That organisms cannot be simulated by any machine. It is not stated in a form that can be measured.
literature: Hundreds of papers; autopoiesis is very widely cited, mostly as an idea.
engineering: Artificial-chemistry and protocell models; an influence on robotics. No everyday use.
admits_open_problems: Its literature argues openly about whether the central theorem holds.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
admits_open_problems: An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.

status.note: Scores are 0 to 3 on the stated scale. A line marked from_memory was not checked against a source tonight. The total is a count of ticks, not a ranking of truth.
